# Assembling Multi-Panel Publication Composites

In peer-reviewed publications, individual analyses are assembled into unified, multi-panel composite figures. This chapter explains how to construct double-column figures conforming to Nature and Science standards using `patchwork`.

## The Double-Column Layout Standard

Leading journals specify standard column widths:
- **Single-Column**: $89.0$ mm ($3.5$ in)
- **1.5-Column**: $120.0\text{--}140.0$ mm ($4.7\text{--}5.5$ in)
- **Double-Column**: $183.0$ mm ($7.2$ in)

`patchwork` combines separate `ggplot2` instances while aligning plot axes and standardizing panel tags (`(a)`, `(b)`, `(c)`).

## Example 1: 3-Panel Systems Biology Composite

```{r composite-assembly-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=7.2}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# Panel A: Node-level cross-network topology
demo_net <- generate_demo_cross_network()
p_a <- cliplot_cross_network_graph(
  nodes       = demo_net$nodes,
  edges       = demo_net$edges,
  cross_edges = demo_net$cross_edges,
  level       = "node",
  preset      = "nature",
  scifig      = TRUE,
  title       = "Cross-Network Modular Architecture"
)

# Panel B: Module comparison overlap matrix
df_nodes <- data.frame(
  Feature     = paste0("Taxon_", 1:60),
  Discovery   = sample(c("M1_Barrier", "M2_Inflammation", "M3_Sebum"), 60, replace = TRUE),
  Replication = sample(c("ModA_Th2", "ModB_Stratum", "ModC_Lipid"), 60, replace = TRUE)
)
p_b <- cliplot(
  Replication ~ Discovery,
  data   = df_nodes,
  type   = type_module_compare(fill_by = "jaccard", show_stars = TRUE),
  preset = "nature",
  title  = "Cross-Network Module Overlap"
)

# Panel C: Coupled environmental network
p_c <- cliplot_env_network(
  title              = "Multi-Domain Environmental Coupling",
  show_values        = TRUE,
  show_domain_labels = TRUE,
  compact            = TRUE,
  preset             = "nature",
  scifig             = TRUE
)

# Assemble using patchwork: Left column (A over B), Right column (C)
p_composite <- (p_a / p_b) | p_c
p_composite <- p_composite +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.0, 1.25)) +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "a",
    tag_prefix = "(",
    tag_suffix = ")",
    theme      = theme(
      plot.tag = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", family = "sans")
    )
  )

p_composite
```

## Example 2: Clinical Trial RECIST Response Composite

Pairing a tumor shrinkage waterfall plot with a treatment duration swimmer plot tracks patient outcome kinetics across a trial cohort:

```{r composite-oncology-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.5}
set.seed(42)
n_pts <- 24

imtrial <- data.frame(
  Patient    = paste0("PT-", sprintf("%02d", 1:n_pts)),
  BestChange = sort(rnorm(n_pts, mean = -22, sd = 32)),
  BestResp   = sample(c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD"), n_pts, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.10, 0.35, 0.35, 0.20)),
  Duration   = pmax(2, round(rnorm(n_pts, mean = 16, sd = 7), 1)),
  Ongoing    = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n_pts, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.4, 0.6))
)

p_wf_comp <- cliplot(
  BestChange ~ Patient,
  data = imtrial,
  type = type_waterfall(
    show_labels         = FALSE,
    bar_width           = 0.68,
    response_thresholds = c("PD" = 20, "PR" = -30)
  ),
  theme = "cell",
  title = "Best Tumor Response"
) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6.0))

p_swim_comp <- cliplot(
  Duration ~ Patient,
  data = imtrial,
  type = type_swimmer(
    bar_fill      = "BestResp",
    ongoing       = "Ongoing",
    bar_linewidth = 3.2
  ),
  theme       = "cell",
  bar_palette = "jama",
  title       = "Treatment Duration"
) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.0))

p_recist_comp <- p_wf_comp + p_swim_comp +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.0, 1.2)) +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "a",
    tag_prefix = "(",
    tag_suffix = ")"
  )

p_recist_comp
```

## Publication Export with `cli_save()` and `cli_journal_size()`

```r
# Export directly to Nature 2-column specifications (183 mm width at 600 DPI)
cli_save(
  p_composite,
  filename   = "Figure_1_Nature.pdf",
  journal    = "nature",
  columns    = "double",
  height_mm  = 180,
  dpi        = 600
)
```
